scope: Adaptive development experiment on already inspected LeFood data, not an independent final evaluation or reproduction of DPF-Nutrition.
hypothesis: Frozen relative-depth shape features add predictive information beyond appearance and imperfect food-mask area.
extraction: EXIF-corrected RGB; pinned official slow image processor with default aspect-preserving resize; frozen local safetensors model, no remote code; resize raw inverse-depth output bilinearly to 256x256 for aligned feature extraction; no labels used.
geometry: Normalize each image by its own 5th/95th depth percentiles. Fit a plane in normalized pixel coordinates to a 15-pixel-wide dilated ring outside the frozen food mask. This ring is not verified plate surface. Record residual shape statistics inside food; missing reference if fewer than 32 ring pixels. Features are dimensionless cues, never grams, metric height or physical volume.
features: Per image: food area; valid-reference flag; signed median and 90th percentile residual; residual std; positive residual sum / image area; positive residual fraction; ring residual std; whole-image normalized depth std. Pair: before, after, after-minus-before. Compare Change baseline, Change+Mask control, Change+Depth, Change+Mask+Depth.
evaluation: Original five LeFood outer test sets and 50-label inner folds, checked for group/component/raw-image boundary overlap. Same 13-candidate group-weighted RBF regression search per new feature family. Standardization fitted only inside each fitting partition. No sample-specific correction, relabeling or exclusions.
selection: Inner group-balanced MAE; gamma {0.5,2,8} x alpha {0.01,0.1,1,10}, plus constant group-weighted median. Clip to [0,1.25].
limitations: Residue/portion confusion cannot be scored without independent visual labels. Recorded zero and small-positive mass slices are proxies with different meaning. Relative depth has per-image scale/shift ambiguity, and pretraining overlap is unknown. All results are conditional development evidence. No automatic deployment.
